chapter: Origins of jazz and the district
title: Jelly Roll Morton, the word jazz and Armstrong and Oliver dates
summary: Brown remembers hearing Morton in Chicago, offers a French derivation for the word jazz, and cites dates for Armstrong and Oliver.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I think this is something I... For some information, I took out of some of the books sometime. In fact, Jelly Roll, Jelly Roll Morton. Well, he happened to be in Chicago. Was, he was 20, and in Chicago in 1905. Born in 1885 in New Orleans. Found in 1941. I guess you got something with that fella, huh? That's it.
Do you remember him? Do you remember him?

Yes, I remember going there and hearing him play. He played a lot of piano. And he used to play singly, mostly. Sometimes he'd play with a little band. But most, many of them had violins. And as I said, the fruits. A different type of music entirely. You couldn't get the color. Did you hear him down here? No, I didn't hear him down here, but up there I did. Now, then I read the origination of jazz. I tried to get it from the library. Of course, they have no records of any word like that before 1950. And then the origination of the word jazz. Now, as a great many writers put it, and all this talk about the, uh, the word jazz being to discredit the orchestra and everything else. Of course, I'm sorry I'll have to differ with Tom in that respect. Wasn't meant at all. It was taken, as I believe, from a French word. A jazzer. A jazzer to pep up. To accelerate. See? That's a French word. And it evidently could have been some French person that used that particular expression. And didn't give it the name of jazz. J-S-S at first. Then later on it was spelled J-A-C. Louis Armstrong was born July the 4th. I just wrote this down a lot of times. Yeah, yeah. And he joined King Oliver's band at Lincoln Garden Cafe in July 1922 in Chicago. So, that's the time he came up there.

That's much later. Joseph King Oliver was born in 1885 on Dryde Street in New Orleans. I guess you saw that in the books. Yeah. Well, I copied a lot of things that I read out of the books in here. The notation. I thought maybe I'd read some of these. Did you ever read Charles Delaney's book?
